standard_prerequisites.use: Basic properties of finite morphisms (closed, affine), the unique-prime-over localization lemma (Algebra, lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below), and elementary localization identities for modules.

core_obligations: Prove the neighbourhood approximation topologically from closedness.
Identify the local ring map with a global localization using uniqueness of the prime above p.
Compare the stalk of F with the stalk of the pushforward.

proof_roadmap.step: Algebraic parts via B_q = B_p and localization of finite presentations.

difficulty_reason: For a finite morphism pi : X -> Y and x over y with pi^{-1}({y}) = {x}, the lemma proves four statements: neighbourhoods of x in X are approximated by full inverse images of neighbourhoods of y; the local ring map O_{Y,y} -> O_{X,x} is finite; it is of finite presentation when pi is; and for every quasi-coherent module F the stalk F_x equals (pi_*F)_y as O_{Y,y}-modules. The retained proof is written: the topological statement from continuity plus closedness of finite maps with the single-point fibre; parts (2), (3) by affinization to a finite ring map A -> B where the fibre condition makes q the unique prime over p, applying Algebra, lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below to identify B_q = B_p so the local map is a plain localization (details the author marks as simple properties of localization); part (4) computed by the same localization identity plus an alternative direct stalk argument via part (1). Retained author proof at lines 13570-13591.
